title: Kessler Garden
description: Glazed porcelain shards fired at different temperatures and arranged by the altitude band each fragment stands in for. A garden of things that will never come down.

title: Low Earth Lace
description: A lace pattern knitted from the tracked positions of 400 objects over one night, read off as stitch density.

title: deorbit.py
description: A small script that takes public orbital data and plays each object's decay as a falling tone. The longer it stays up, the lower it sings.

title: Fairing, Flat-Pack
description: Cut files for a rocket nose-cone fairing redrawn as a flat-pack storage box. Every curve is kept, every bolt hole becomes a hinge.

title: Re-entry Stool
description: An 18 mm MDF stool cut from offcuts of three other projects. The legs splay at the angle a capsule meets the atmosphere.

title: Tracking 27,000
description: A live sketch that draws one dot for every catalogued object and lets you switch off the ones still working. Most of the sky stays lit.

title: Spent Stage
description: A scanned upper stage reduced to a low-poly shell and printed at 1:50, then left outside for a month to weather.

title: The Graveyard Orbit
description: Plans for a station built 300 km above geostationary orbit, where old satellites are parked to die. Who designs the cemetery?

title: Ablative
description: Outerwear built from heat-shield logic: layers meant to char and flake away so the wearer stays intact.

title: Signal Loss
description: A three-minute film assembled from frames that dropped out of a satellite feed. The gaps are the story.

title: Ghost Satellites
description: Recordings of radio beacons from satellites that have been dead for decades but still transmit when sunlight hits their panels.

title: Collision Avoidance Manual
description: A fictional operations manual for a single person whose only job is to keep two pieces of junk from touching. Forty pages, no plot.

title: Shield Panels
description: Perforated MDF wall panels patterned after Whipple shields, the thin layers that break up debris before it reaches a hull.

title: Point Nemo
description: A poster series about the spacecraft cemetery in the South Pacific, the place on Earth furthest from any land.

title: Tether Knots
description: Rings modelled on failed space tether experiments. Each one is a knot that should have held.

title: Kessler Cascade
description: A collision simulation you can run in the browser. Add one more satellite and watch the chain reaction start.

title: Orbital Census
description: Risograph prints listing every launch from one year, sorted by what is still up there.

title: Drag Sail
description: A folding sail that deploys at end of life to pull a small satellite down faster. Drawings, fold tests and a 1:1 prototype.

title: Fragments per km³
description: A type specimen where letter weight follows debris density at each altitude. The heaviest weight sits at 800 km.

title: Return Capsule Room
description: A room the size of a return capsule, modelled for one person to spend an hour in. Most visitors leave early.

title: Paint Fleck
description: Large canvases about a fleck of paint small enough to crack a shuttle window. Mostly empty, slightly scratched.

title: Flyby, Loop
description: Long exposures of the night sky over London, cut into a loop where satellites trace the same lines again and again.

title: Space Junk Lamp
description: A lamp made of laser-cut MDF rings that you stack in any order. No two assemblies give the same shadow.

title: Telemetry Hum
description: A drone piece built from the data rate of one weather satellite across a single orbit.
